description: A project's Devbox recipe: what one branch workspace runs (apps, Compose services, scripts), never ports or hosts. It lives at the project repo's root; `devbox config check` lints it against the checkout, `devbox config check --static` against the file alone.

build.description: Build: optional build command for `devbox deploy`.

cmd.description: Cmd: the long-running command; {port:<name>} expands to the allocated absolute port, {port} to the app's first port.

deps.description: Deps: the dependency step keyed on lockfile content (conf.Deps). On the SYNCED app, like provision.

cmd.description: Cmd: the installer, run in the app's synced checkout — the project's own (FixIt: bash scripts/ci/install-workspace-dependencies.sh), never a bare package-manager call that picks another layout.

key.description: Key: files relative to the app's checkout, e.g. [bun.lock, package.json, "apps/*/package.json"]; a single-segment glob (filepath.Match) may name several. Hashed in the guest tree after the sync flush.

profile.description: Profile: the test resource profile the refresh runs under; default small, and never larger than the recipe's resources.test envelope.

provision_installs.description: ProvisionInstalls: the app's provision runs Cmd unconditionally, so a provision that passed in an up IS the first install — up records the key's hash instead of installing again. Explicit on purpose: provision text that merely contains Cmd (echoed, or behind a condition that skipped it) is no proof the installer ran.

env_file.description: EnvFile: secret env file name under the workspace's box env dir, seeded via `devbox env push`, never in git. A process sources it; a source_only app keeps it for its post_seed or Compose stack to read.

ports.description: Ports: named ports this app binds, in declared order. Offsets within the workspace window are assigned across the recipe deterministically.

post_seed.description: PostSeed: a command run in this SYNCED app's checkout after EVERY seed_files push — each up (after its provisions) and each run, --no-up included — because every push lands the Mac's raw copies again while provision is hash-gated. It keeps box-side rewrites of seeded files (port and host remaps) in place. It must be idempotent, fast and free of runtime topology: a --no-up run has no leased ports or data slot, so only {workspace}, {namespace} and {state} expand. A failure stops the verb with WS_POST_SEED_FAILED.

profiles.description: Profiles makes the app opt-in. It remains part of deterministic port allocation, but is only synthesized when one of these profiles is active.

provision.description: Provision: one-time setup run in the app's synced checkout by `ws up` after the first sync, before units start. Same {port:<name>} expansion as cmd. Marker-gated; see conf.App.Provision.

run_in.description: RunIn: name of a synced sibling app whose checkout this process runs in (the monorepo shape: one synced tree, several processes). Mutually exclusive with sync; the app is not synced itself.

seed_files.description: SeedFiles copies ignored, machine-local files from the primary checkout after source sync and before provision. This is the declarative bridge for development credentials: recipes name paths, while Devbox validates and copies them mode 0600 without ever printing their contents.

source.description: Source accepts main:<relative-path> for the root project's primary checkout or sync:<relative-path> for this app's resolved checkout. The explicit origin prevents feature-worktree output from becoming accidental credential truth while letting every sibling repo own its own config.

target.description: Target is relative to this app's synced checkout in the guest.

source_only.description: SourceOnly syncs a repository into the workspace without creating a process or consuming a port. Native Compose and sibling apps may use it.

sync.description: Sync: "." (or empty) = the invoking worktree; an absolute/~ path pins another Mac directory. sibling:<repo> uses its primary checkout; paired:<repo> prefers its checkout on the invoking branch, otherwise primary. Instantiation resolves it.

sync_ignores.description: SyncIgnores: mirror the essentials of the repo's .gitignore — the generator must never read the synced tree at render time (hermeticity, PR #110).

apps.description: Apps: bare processes devbox runs as systemd user units, mutagen-synced from the Mac worktree. Port NAMES here; numbers are allocated per workspace and injected via {port:<name>} expansion (decision 6).

compose.description: Compose is the native whole-stack contract. Unlike an opaque compose list, every service is declared so Devbox can reset all published ports and namespace every container before anything starts.

memory.description: Memory is the Compose services' share of the stack's memory need ("1G"), for a stack that also runs native apps: admission charges only this part against devbox-docker.slice and the rest against the host. Unset charges the whole need to the slice, an upper bound for its Compose part.

ready_timeout.description: ReadyTimeout bounds up's wait for every service to run (a one-shot to exit 0) after a start, as a duration ("8m"); unset is DefaultComposeReadyTimeout. A stack whose first start runs long one-shots (migrations, seeding) declares what that start takes.

ports.description: Ports maps Devbox's stable name to the container port. Host ports are allocated from the workspace window and never accepted as input.

restart.description: Restart overrides the safe on-failure default for processes which may exit cleanly during dependency warm-up and must be retried by Docker. It holds only while the stack runs: `always` renders as unless-stopped (a daemon restart revives `always` after any stop), a parked stack is disarmed to `no`, and compose-run re-arms the policy on up.

data_init.description: DataInit names the scripts entry devbox runs once on a fresh data set: right after the up whose start found every Compose volume of the workspace absent or empty (a new workspace, a --no-data move's target), through the same run path as `devbox run <script>`, with the stack up. A volume holding data is never fresh, and the pending marker is taken before the run, so a non-idempotent seeder runs at most once (ws/data_init.go). Refused on a source: native recipe.

data_init_paths.description: DataInitPaths are datastore bind directories relative to {state}. They are surveyed before the first start, never the whole state tree.

datasets.description: Datasets are loaded from the store into a fresh workspace; Volumes marks Compose volumes regenerable — neither is copied by a move or a cold park (datasets.go).

docs.description: Docs names the project's own devbox notes (a Markdown file relative to this recipe's directory): what an agent reads before operating the project. It lives in the project, never in Devbox's skill; config check, setup and status hand it out as data.context.docs. An older CLI's strict decode refuses the key, never ignores it.

onyx.description: Onyx is the vault item holding this account (onyx://<project>/<item>): the Onyx browser extension fills the sign-in form from it, and an agent signs in with web_login.

role.description: Role names what the account is for (admin, approver), unique per address, lowercase [a-z0-9-].

shared.description: Shared marks an account that also exists outside the workspace (a shared identity provider, a deployed tenant): its password is the Onyx item's, never DevPassword, so a shared row requires onyx.

user.description: User is what the sign-in form's user field takes.

logins.description: Logins are the test accounts a person or an agent signs in with, keyed by the address name `devbox url` prints (an app, or a Compose port key). `devbox url` and the ready block hand them out beside the address. An older CLI's strict decode refuses the key, never ignores it.

requires.description: Requires names box capabilities the workspace needs (boxes.yaml `provides`): registry-mirror, litellm, forge-ai, committed-band, pwf-shared, portal. Placement only considers boxes providing every one; a recipe requiring nothing lands wherever headroom is best.

resources.description: Resources selects centrally-owned workspace and test envelopes. A command override never changes these limits.

memory.description: Memory is the project's ESTIMATED hot footprint ("6G"), not a limit: admission subtracts it from headroom, the hot ceiling sums it across running stacks, and the sweep reports drift against the measured slice peak (2026-09-02 memory-pressure decisions 9/10). The profile ceilings above stay the enforced envelope.

profile.description: Profile is the test resource profile this script runs under when the run names none (`--resource-profile` beats it): small, medium, standard or heavy, never past the recipe's resources.test envelope (decodeRecipe refuses it). Empty runs under the envelope itself.

stdin_refs.description: StdinRefs maps JSON fields to Onyx refs. The Mac injects them into the guest's stdin; no values belong in a recipe or a workspace env file.

up.description: Nil preserves existing recipes' app-start behavior. False prepares only source sync; the command is still admitted against its RAM profile.

scripts.description: Scripts: named entry points (`test`, `migrate`, `seed`, …) of arbitrary shell run by `devbox run <name>` inside the workspace's synced checkout. Same {port:<name>} expansion as app cmds. Devbox is use-agnostic about what a script does — only non-empty is enforced. A scalar is the command; the mapping form `{cmd, image}` pins the command inside a container image (see Script).

shared.description: Shared names Devbox-managed or externally-owned services required by every instance of this recipe. Names intentionally match Compose service names so an agent can move between both models without a translation table.

shared_topology.description: SharedTopology is how a checkout reaches the project's shared data topology (its devbox.shared.yaml): "opt-in" (absent: by hand, `devbox config reservine-shared --apply`) or "born-shared" (a workspace that never started opts in before its first start — ws/reservine_born_shared.go, docs/specs/2026-10-09-reservine-born-shared-decisions.md). Reservine only. An older CLI's strict decode refuses the key, never ignores it.

system_packages.description: SystemPackages derives the guest apt packages the project needs from its production Dockerfile (system_packages.go); the box warns about the ones it lacks.

apt.description: Apt: Ubuntu noble names no Dockerfile carries — test-only tools, or the translation of an apk/other-distro stage the parser refuses.

except.description: Except: container-only or build-time names (an init like dumb-init, an installer's unzip) the guest does not need.

from.description: From: Dockerfiles, clean paths relative to the invoking worktree.

uses.description: Uses: shared-services.yaml refs — infra consumed, never owned. Deprecated: use shared.required. Kept so existing recipes remain valid.

verify.description: Verify names the scripts a verdict runs, each its own admitted run (recipe_verify.go); Schedule the scripts run on a cron. Neither ever reaches conf.Workspace, so editing them never restarts a stack, and the typed worktree patch cannot express them. Decode checks their shape only — VerifyProblems/ScheduleProblems the references — so a gate typo never breaks up or run.
